caps.text: One day, the last star in this universe will go out
Scientists have three different paths for the end of the universe
and the 2026 data has turned the game around
The final fate of every galaxy, every planet and every living thing hides in these three paths
And the three outcomes are completely different
In the first, space expands so fast that every atom bursts into pieces
In the second, everything goes cold as ice
and even the last black hole disappears
In the third, the whole universe shrinks back and swallows itself
Which path we take is in the hands of a force discovered in 1998
In the 1990s, two separate teams of astronomers were watching exploding stars in distant galaxies
Saul Perlmutter, Brian Schmidt and Adam Riess used the light of these Type Ia supernova explosions to measure the speed of the universe
Until then, every scientist believed the expansion of the universe was slowing down
The logic was simple
Throw a cricket ball straight up, and Earth's gravity pulls it back down
It slows as it rises, stops for a moment, and falls back to the ground
Scientists thought galaxies must be doing exactly the same
After the Big Bang everything is flying apart, but gravity must be pulling it back
But when the 1998 data came up on the computer screen, the whole calculation came out backwards
The distant supernova explosions looked much dimmer than expected
It meant those galaxies were moving away, and their speed was rising instead of falling
As if the cricket ball kept speeding up in the air
It made no sense
Scientists named the unknown force behind this strange acceleration dark energy
Today, about 68 percent of the whole universe is thought to be this dark energy
For this discovery, the three scientists won the 2011 Nobel Prize in Physics
Interestingly, Albert Einstein had thought of such a force back in 1917
He added a number called the cosmological constant to his equations
But in 1929 Edwin Hubble showed that the universe is expanding
Einstein dropped it
Later, physicist George Gamow claimed Einstein called it his biggest blunder
But Einstein's own papers hold no such evidence
Either way, after 1998 that old idea came back to the centre of science
Now the biggest question was: what happens if dark energy grows stronger?
In 2003, physicist Robert Caldwell and two colleagues solved a frightening equation
Until then it was believed that however strong dark energy was, galaxies would always hold together
because gravity inside galaxies is strong enough
But Caldwell's team worked out a different kind of dark energy, called phantom energy
If the density of dark energy kept rising with time, gravity's grip would begin to loosen
They called it the Big Rip
THE BIG RIP
By the Planck satellite's data, even if it happens, it would take at least 200 billion years
First, the big galaxy clusters will separate and scatter
Then even lone galaxies like the Milky Way won't keep their shape
EVERY ORBIT BREAKS
Every orbit will break
Stars will wander into the dark, and in the last few months planets will be pulled away from their stars
A few minutes before the end, planets and stars will burst apart from inside
In less than the last second, space will grow faster than light
Even the nuclear force that holds atoms together will give up
Every atom will tear apart
Space will grow so fast that no particle can ever reach another
Each particle will be left as a lonely universe of its own
But most scientists think phantom energy probably doesn't exist at all
In their view the universe won't rip apart. It will slowly cool down and fall silent
In 1852, British physicist Lord Kelvin painted a different picture of the end of the universe
His calculation rested on a basic law of thermodynamics, known today as entropy
Every hot thing shares its heat and cools down
A hot cup of chai left in a room reaches room temperature in a few minutes
The whole universe is on exactly the same road
HEAT DEATH
That is the Heat Death
Here space keeps expanding, and galaxies drift so far away they can no longer be seen
The gas clouds needed to make new stars slowly run out
Scientists estimate the last star will go out in about 100 trillion years
After that, only black holes and cold dead stars will be left in the dark
Black holes seemed immortal
But in 1974 Stephen Hawking showed that black holes slowly lose their energy too
This is called Hawking radiation
The biggest supermassive black holes will take about ten to the power 100 years to vanish completely
For years everyone thought white dwarfs and neutron stars would last even longer
Their lifetime was put at ten to the power 1,100 years
But in May 2025, Dutch physicist Heino Falcke and his team changed that calculation
MAY 2025
Their equations showed that everything with gravity slowly evaporates away
EVEN THE MOON
The Moon too, and neutron stars too
By this count, the last white dwarf stars will be gone in ten to the power 78 years
In the end the whole universe will be evenly cold and silent, where nothing ever changes
For decades, Heat Death was seen as the surest ending
But a telescope on a mountain in Arizona cracked that certainty
On Kitt Peak in the Arizona desert stands a four-metre telescope called the Mayall Telescope
KITT PEAK, ARIZONA
Inside it sits a special instrument called DESI
DESI has 5,000 small optical fibres that catch the light of thousands of galaxies at once
In the last five years it has mapped more than 47 million galaxies and quasars in 3D
Its goal was clear
Scientists wanted to measure the strength of dark energy better than ever
Everyone expected dark energy to come out perfectly constant, like Einstein's cosmological constant
But the data from 2024 to 2026 showed a different pattern
The signals suggest dark energy may be weakening
There are hints its strength has dropped by about ten percent over the last few billion years
This is not a confirmed discovery yet
Physicists are waiting for more data to check it fully
But if this hint turns out true, the universe won't end in Heat Death
SEPTEMBER 2025
In September 2025, Cornell physicist Henry Tye and colleagues built a model on this same data
By their calculation, the universe's whole life may be about 33 billion years
Right now it is 13.8 billion years old
So it has already lived about half its life
In this model the universe reaches its largest size in the next 11 billion years, then stops
Then dark energy gives up, and gravity takes control again
After about 20 billion years, the whole universe would shrink back into a single point
An Indian physicist's equations show this crash would not be the final stop
If dark energy really weakens, the expansion will stop and run backwards
Galaxies will come racing towards each other
As space shrinks, the temperature of the whole universe keeps rising
It gets hotter everywhere
In the last stage of the collapse, radiation in space gets so hot that stars begin melting from the outside
Then black holes will collide and merge with each other
In the final moment, the whole universe shrinks into a tiny point
Scientists call this the Big Crunch
THE BIG CRUNCH
In the old physics, density becomes infinite at this point and everything ends
INFINITE
Einstein's general relativity stops working here
But Maharashtra-born physicist Abhay Ashtekar saw this final moment differently
Working on Loop Quantum Cosmology, he brought quantum mechanics and gravity together
His equations gave a strange result
In this theory, space is built from tiny quantum pieces
So when the universe shrinks down to a limit, it can't be squeezed any further
At that limit, gravity starts pushing instead of pulling
And from there the whole universe bounces back outward
This is called the Big Bounce
THE BIG BOUNCE
So the Big Bang that began our universe may have been the end of an earlier one
There is no direct proof of this theory yet, because such conditions can't be created in a lab
Nobody yet has the final truth about dark energy
Science hasn't decided whether this force stays the same forever or slowly fades away
If it stays constant, the universe will cool down over trillions of years and fall silent forever
And if it is weakening, gravity will gather everything back and begin a different universe
The verdict is still open
The darkness of the last star, where this story began,
may become the first light of the next sky
